candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 4:17 (Enoch as scribe (4:17)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And he was the first among men that are born on earth who learnt writing and knowledge and wisdom and who wrote down the signs of heaven according to the order of their months in a book, that men might know the seasons of the years according to the order of their separate months' — Enoch as the FIRST scribe of wisdom. Jubilees and 1 Enoch agree on this point (cf. 1En 12:4). Tewahedo manuscript tradition explicitly traces its theological lineage to this Enochic scribal commissioning: every monastic scribe stands in the Enochic succession.

candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 4:23 (Enoch translated (4:23)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour, and behold there he writeth down the condemnation and judgement of the world, and all the wickedness of the children of men' — Enoch translated to Eden (not heaven directly, as 1 En 71 has it). Jubilees locates Enoch's translation in the Garden, where he continues to write. Tewahedo Edenic-monastic-theology preserves the Edenic-garden as still ACCESSIBLE in some sense for the holy: the monk's cell is a fragmentary participation in the Edenic Enochic geography.
